title: Why Is KDP Rejecting My EPUB? (And How to Fix It)
excerpt: KDP rejection emails are vague. 'Your file could not be published' doesn't tell you much. This guide covers the seven most common KDP EPUB rejection reasons with specific fixes for each.

meta_description: KDP rejecting your EPUB with vague error messages? This guide covers the 7 most common rejection reasons and gives you exact steps to fix each one before re-uploading.
html:
You've finished your book. You've spent hours formatting it. You upload to KDP and get back a rejection with a two-sentence error message that tells you almost nothing.

KDP rejecting an EPUB is incredibly common, and the error messages are notoriously vague. "Your file could not be published due to content errors" — okay, but which file? Which content? Where?

Here are the seven most common reasons KDP rejects EPUB files and what to do about each one.

Reason 1: Broken EPUB Package Structure

The EPUB package structure has strict requirements. The file must be a valid ZIP archive containing a mimetype file as the first item, an uncompressed META-INF/container.xml file that points to the OPF, and the actual EPUB content in a folder.

Where this breaks: when authors create EPUBs by renaming a ZIP file or using a ZIP tool that compresses the mimetype file or includes the top-level folder.

Fix: Use an EPUB-specific tool to repackage. If you're doing it manually, add the mimetype file first using the store(no compression) method, then add everything else. Run the result through the EPUB Validator to confirm the package structure passes before re-uploading to KDP.

Reason 2: No Table of Contents Detected

KDP requires a navigable table of contents. Your EPUB needs either an NCX file (for EPUB 2.0) or a nav document with epub:type="toc" (for EPUB 3.0). If these are missing, broken, or not listed correctly in the OPF manifest, KDP blocks the upload.

Fix: Generate a proper TOC from your chapter headings using the TOC Generator. Make sure the resulting TOC file is listed in the OPF manifest and that the spine order is correct. For EPUB 3.0, the nav document also needs properties="nav" in its manifest item.

Reason 3: Malformed XML in Content Files

KDP parses every HTML content file in your EPUB as XHTML. XHTML is stricter than regular HTML — it's valid XML, which means every tag must be closed, attribute values must be quoted, and special characters must be escaped.

One unclosed <img> tag can cause a parse failure for the entire chapter file. An ampersand in a URL (&) that isn't escaped as & is an XML error.

Fix: Run your EPUB through the EPUB Validator. It identifies every XML error by filename and line number. Fix each one in a text editor, repackage, and re-upload. If the errors are widespread — dozens of files with hundreds of errors — a full rebuild from your manuscript is faster than manual patching.

Reason 4: Missing or Incorrect Metadata

Your OPF file must contain valid metadata: a unique identifier (usually an ISBN or UUID), a dc:title, a dc:language in valid BCP 47 format (like en or en-US), and a dc:creator. Missing or invalid metadata causes KDP to reject the file.

A common mistake is setting dc:language to something like "English" instead of the proper language code "en". KDP parses this value strictly.

Fix: Open your OPF file and verify each required metadata element. Use the Metadata Builder to generate properly formatted metadata that you can paste directly into your OPF file — no guessing about the right format.

Reason 5: Image Errors

KDP will reject or warn about images that are referenced in your HTML but don't exist in the EPUB package. It will also reject certain image formats — EPUB supports JPEG, PNG, GIF, and SVG. WEBP images and other formats will cause errors.

Another common issue: image paths in your HTML use absolute paths or incorrect relative paths. If your chapter file is in OEBPS/Text/chapter1.xhtml and your image is in OEBPS/Images/cover.jpg, the relative path in your HTML should be ../Images/cover.jpg — not Images/cover.jpg or an absolute path.

Fix: Validate your EPUB to get a list of broken image references. Fix path issues in the HTML files, convert any non-supported image formats to JPEG or PNG, and ensure every referenced image is included in the package and listed in the OPF manifest.

Reason 6: DRM or Encryption Conflicts

If you're uploading a file that was previously DRM-protected by another platform, KDP will reject it. EPUBs downloaded from Kobo, Google Play, or other retailers are DRM-locked and cannot be re-uploaded to KDP.

This also applies to test files downloaded from KDP itself — they have KDP DRM applied and can't be re-uploaded. Always upload from your original source file, not from a copy downloaded from a store.

Reason 7: Embedded Fonts Without Proper Licensing or Declaration

KDP allows embedded fonts, but they must be declared in the OPF manifest and in the EPUB's encryption file if they're obfuscated. Embedded fonts that aren't properly declared cause structural errors. Fonts that are embedded without a license that permits embedding can cause content policy rejections, not just structural ones.

Fix: Use only fonts with licenses that explicitly allow embedding (SIL Open Font License, for example). Declare embedded fonts in your OPF manifest with media-type="application/vnd.ms-opentype" or application/font-woff as appropriate. Remove any fonts that shouldn't be embedded and reference system fonts instead.

The Fastest Way to Diagnose Any KDP Rejection

Stop guessing from the rejection email. Upload your EPUB to the BookKraft AI EPUB Validator first. It runs the same structural checks that KDP runs — checking mimetype, container, OPF, manifest, spine, HTML validity, image references, and TOC — and gives you a specific, prioritized list of problems.

Fix the problems the validator identifies, re-validate to confirm they're resolved, then upload to KDP. You'll get through in one attempt instead of several.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know if my rejection is technical or content-related?

Technical rejections appear within a few minutes of upload and cite file structure, format, or metadata issues. Content rejections appear after 24–72 hours of review and cite policy violations. If your rejection arrived in under 10 minutes, it's almost certainly technical.

Can I use EPUB 2.0 for KDP?

Yes, KDP accepts EPUB 2.0. But EPUB 3.0 is the current standard, supports more features, and is less likely to trigger formatting warnings. If you're creating a new EPUB, build to EPUB 3.0 spec.

Does the KDP Previewer catch all errors before upload?

No. The KDP Previewer shows how your book renders on Kindle devices but doesn't perform full EPUB validation. A file can look correct in the previewer and still fail KDP's upload validator. Run a separate EPUB validator before using the KDP Previewer.

My EPUB worked on KDP before. Why is it being rejected now?

KDP occasionally tightens its validation requirements. A file that passed a year ago may fail today because KDP has updated its parser or added new checks. Run the file through a current validator to see if any previously-tolerated errors are now being flagged.

How many times can I re-upload to KDP after a rejection?

There's no hard limit on re-uploads. But fix all known issues before each attempt — don't upload again until your validator shows zero errors. Repeated failed uploads on the same title can slow your review processing time.
